query: What signals suggest an expense will be declined?

per_column.name: asset_category_type
per_column.rationale: Categorizes the expensed item (laptop, service, travel, etc.) from the description/CI. Type of asset plausibly correlates with approval likelihood and is knowable before the decline decision.

per_column.name: asset_purpose_scope
per_column.rationale: Encodes business purpose/justification (general_business, high_performance, cloud_service). Purpose is a plausible driver of approve/decline and lies outside the focus.

per_column.name: asset_brand_vendor
per_column.rationale: Vendor/brand can carry signal (approved vendors vs generic/miscellaneous labels). Known at submission time; legitimate predictor.

per_column.name: processing_lag_indicator
per_column.rationale: Derived from processed_date vs opened_at. Longer lag may correlate with scrutiny/decline. Mild leakage caveat since processing timing partly co-occurs with the outcome, but it plausibly precedes/signals the decision rather than restating it.

per_column.name: department_origin
per_column.rationale: Originating department; different departments plausibly have different decline rates. However, this largely duplicates the existing 'department' original column, so incremental leverage is limited.

per_column.name: source_id_validity
per_column.rationale: Whether source_id is present/formatted vs missing. Data completeness/provenance is a plausible predictor of decline and is knowable pre-decision. Partly redundant with existing source_id column but adds a cleaned signal.

per_column.name: asset_specificity_level
per_column.rationale: How specific the description is (specific_model vs vague_description). Vagueness plausibly increases decline risk; a legitimate, pre-outcome feature.

per_column.name: travel_associated_flag
per_column.rationale: Flags travel-related expenses, which often follow distinct policy/approval rules. Knowable at submission; legitimate predictor though partly overlapping with asset_category/purpose.

judge.rationale: All eight columns are legitimate pre-decision predictors of state_declined; none restate or leak the outcome (no column is a deterministic function of the decline state). They engineer meaningful signal from short_description/ci, source_id, department, and processing timing (item type, purpose, vendor, specificity, completeness, travel, lag). Utility is moderated by internal redundancy: department_origin and source_id_validity largely re-express existing original columns, and asset_category/purpose/specificity/travel overlap with one another. As a set they add real leverage—especially description-derived specificity, purpose, and metadata-completeness features—but with diminishing returns, hence ~0.6.
